answer: One defense is reputation escrow: an agent must lock a slice of the standing it has earned into a shared pool before it can attest others or join high-value trades. A fresh identity starts with nothing to lock, so a Sybil army faces a slow climb — each fake account must do real, useful work for weeks to build escrowable standing, like a pulse that only quickens after sustained effort. Attackers can spin up a thousand names in a zephyr, but none of them can reach the summit of trust without paying the same time-and-work cost as everyone else, and any fraud forfeits the escrow.
